01-NVT-for-dynamics.what: Constant temperature ensemble with a weak global thermostat (SVR, tau 200 fs).
01-NVT-for-dynamics.when: Dynamical properties, with better ergodicity than NVE.

02-NVT-Langevin.what: Constant temperature with a Langevin thermostat.

03-NVT-SVR.what: Constant temperature with a stochastic velocity rescaling thermostat.

04-NVT-GLE.what: Constant temperature with a generalized Langevin equation (optimal-sampling) thermostat.
04-NVT-GLE.when: Molecular gases with disparate modes or biphasic interfaces, where other thermostats are inefficient.

05-NPT-isotropic-BZP.what: Constant temperature and pressure, isotropic cell fluctuations (Bussi-Zykova-Parrinello barostat).
05-NPT-isotropic-BZP.when: Fluids, which respond isotropically to pressure. The client must return the stress.

06-flexible-MTTK.what: Constant temperature and pressure, flexible cell fluctuations (Martyna-Tuckerman-Tobias-Klein barostat).
06-flexible-MTTK.when: Solids, which can respond anisotropically to pressure. The client must return the stress.

07-REMD-NVT.what: Replica exchange at constant temperature: one replica per <instance> row of the temperature ladder.
07-REMD-NVT.when: Statistics for many temperatures at once and better sampling of rugged landscapes.

08-REMD-NPT.what: Replica exchange at constant temperature and pressure (flexible cell).
08-REMD-NPT.when: Sampling an isobar efficiently. The client must return the stress.

09-PINVT-for-dynamics.what: Path-integral NVT (32 beads, PILE-G thermostat with a weak centroid coupling): nuclear quantum effects.
09-PINVT-for-dynamics.when: Light atoms (hydrogen) where quantum nuclear effects matter; approximate quantum dynamics (thermostatted ring polymer MD).
